notes: Key convention: `majors` is an object (not an array) keyed by "llvm-<major>", "gcc-<major>", or the fixed key "msvc-redist-14.x" -- this deviates from the generic SCHEMA.md example (an array of {major, ...} objects) because this file covers three toolchain families (LLVM/Clang, GCC via WinLibs/w64devkit/GCC-source, and the MSVC redistributable) sharing one file per the SCHEMA.md instruction ('one file per language family folder'). The `gcc` runtime major in releases.json/gaps.json is the BUNDLED GCC version regardless of which of the three GCC distribution projects (WinLibs, w64devkit, GCC source tarballs) produced it; a single 'gcc-<major>' entry here covers all three for that major, and os_support notes where they differ (WinLibs/w64devkit ship Windows binaries with an MSVCRT-vs-UCRT runtime choice; GCC source is build-it-yourself with no official binary for any OS). The 'gcc-various' key corresponds to the single gaps.json row for the defunct mingw-builds (niXman) SourceForge project and carries no real research, only a placeholder. LLVM majors 21-23 postdate this research pass's ability to independently cross-check secondary sources (WebFetch pulled the live, current clang.llvm.org/gcc.gnu.org pages, which speak in aggregated version ranges rather than confirming each individual recent major), so their `added`/`limitations`/`os_support` are marked confidence: low and are best-effort extrapolations, not vendor-confirmed per-version facts.

msvc-redist-14.x.released: 2015-present (VS2015 through current VS2022/2026 -- all share the ABI-compatible 'v140' runtime line)
added: single binary-compatible runtime line since VS2015: vc_redist.x64/x86/arm64.exe installs vcruntime140.dll, msvcp140.dll etc. and later VS versions only ever ADD side-by-side versioned DLLs (140_1, 140_2, ...), never break the v140 ABI
limitations: this is a REDISTRIBUTABLE RUNTIME, not a compiler -- it does not itself gate which C/C++ standard your code can use; that's determined by the cl.exe (MSVC) version used to build, which is outside this catalog
installing the latest vc_redist does not retroactively add e.g. /std:c++20 language support to an old cl.exe
ARM64 vc_redist only became available well after x86/x64 (Windows on ARM support matured through VS2017-2019)
no static-linking equivalent shipped via redist -- static CRT linking requires the full VS build tools, not the redist package

os_support.windows: practical floor is Windows 7 SP1 with the Platform Update (KB2670838) for the earliest v140 (VS2015) redist; current vc_redist.x64.exe (aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe) states Windows 10 or later as the supported target, though it has been reported to still install on 7/8.1 in practice
